title: Strongly transcendental element
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $x\in S$. The element $x$ is *strongly transcendental over $R$* if for every $u\in S$ and every polynomial $P=a_0+a_1X+\dots+a_kX^k\in R[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] the equality $u\,(\varphi(a_0)+\varphi(a_1)x+\dots+\varphi(a_k)x^k)=0$ in $S$ implies $u\,\varphi(a_i)=0$ for all $i=0,\dots,k$. When $\varphi$ is the inclusion of a subring $R\subseteq S$ this reads: $u(a_0+a_1x+\dots+a_kx^k)=0$ with $u\in S$, $a_i\in R$ implies $ua_i=0$ for all $i$.
